content.title: About
content.content: Bread is a staple food made by baking a dough of flour, water, yeast and salt. Spanish coffee is a fragrant beverage prepared from roasted Arabica beans, often served as espresso or "café con leche".

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Spanish bread "pan" often has a crunchy crust and a soft crumb.
In Spain, "café con leche" and "café solo" are popular and served in small cups.
Spanish coffee plantations are located in the Canary Islands, where the climate suits Arabica cultivation.
Mediterranean breads are frequently enriched with olive oil and rosemary.
Coffee in Spain is commonly accompanied by sweet pastries such as churros.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Bread provides a quick supply of carbohydrates, while coffee stimulates metabolism thanks to caffeine.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Especially whole‑grain flour contains vitamins B1, B3 and B6, important for the nervous system.

items.title: Antioxidants in coffee
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Caffeine speeds intestinal motility, and whole‑grain bread supplies dietary fiber.

items.title: Improves concentration
items.content: Caffeine enhances alertness and cognitive performance.

items.title: Gluten sensitivity
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten intolerance may experience serious symptoms from bread.

items.title: Excess caffeine intake
items.content: High doses of coffee can cause anxiety, insomnia and rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar and salt content
items.content: Some breads and ready‑to‑drink coffee beverages contain added sugar and salt, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Acidity of coffee
items.content: The acidic nature of coffee may irritate the stomach in individuals with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread can be enjoyed fresh, toasted, as sandwiches, or used in recipes. Spanish coffee is typically served hot as espresso, "café con leche" or "café americano". Pair bread with olive oil, cheese, ham or sweet spreads, and coffee with desserts such as churros.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bread in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage, freeze bread in an airtight bag. Keep coffee in a sealed container away from light, moisture and heat; a dark pantry is ideal.
